sentence_stem: If I had studied harder last year,
correct_completion: I would have a better job now.
full_sentence: If I had studied harder last year, I would have a better job now.
acceptable_variants: I would be earning more money now.
My career would be going much better today.

options.text: I will have a better job next week.
options.why_wrong: 'Will' describes a future plan. A mixed conditional needs 'would' to show the present result of a past condition.

options.text: I have a better job now.
options.why_wrong: This states a real present fact. It does not express the imagined result of a past condition that did not happen.

options.text: I would have a better job now.

options.why_wrong: This describes a past activity, but it does not complete the result clause that a conditional needs.

grammar_focus: Mixed conditionals (past condition with present result)
explanation: The 'if' clause refers to a past situation, so it uses the past perfect 'had studied'. The result clause refers to the present, so it uses 'would' with a present-time reference, creating a mixed conditional.
